checked_and_fine: day_signed_ratio (partura/ops_ext.py:120): kernel computes exactly sum(|y|*sign(x))/sum(|y|) over jointly-finite minutes as its own docstring states (sign(0)=0 correctly makes x==0 count in the denominator only). Verified element-by-element against an independent per-minute-loop reference (not the kernel's vectorized style) across random / 10-30% NaN / all-NaN-row / all-NaN-column / constant / 5-value-tie / mixed-sign inputs, magnitudes 1e-9..1e16, float32 and float64, D,S,M up to (4,4,241), plus a dedicated large-magnitude (up to 1e16) low-dispersion stress test on y: all matched (float32 vs float64 differ by <=1e-6, normal rounding). day_gini (partura/ops_ext.py:134): the sort-and-rank-weighted formula (2*sum(i*x_(i))/(n*sum(x)) - (n+1)/n) was cross-checked against a completely independent O(n^2) double-sum mean-absolute-difference Gini reference across the full scenario matrix (same list as day_signed_ratio) including D=1,S=1,M=1 degenerate shapes. Matches to float64 machine precision everywhere except an exact-zero-reference 'constant row' case, where both kernel and a from-scratch float64 reference differ from mathematical 0 only at the ~1e-16 (float64) / ~1.2e-7 (float32) machine-epsilon floor -- ordinary floating-point rounding on any correct implementation, not a logic error (confirmed separately: feeding a 5e8-magnitude row with genuine jitter down to exactly 0 keeps float32 within ~3.6e-7 of float64 throughout, no blow-up). No cross-day leakage.

day_centroid (partura/ops_ext.py:153): sum(t*|x|)/sum(|x|)/(T-1) verified by an independent loop reference across the full scenario matrix including T=1 and T=2 degenerate minute widths and T=241; abs() is applied identically to numerator and denominator in the kernel, matching the docstring. Matches within ordinary float32/float64 rounding (<=4e-7) at every magnitude tested, including the same large-magnitude (5e8, jitter down to 0) low-dispersion stress that broke cross_zscore -- day_centroid shows no comparable blow-up because its formula has no near-zero-divided-by-near-zero structure. Specifically replayed the historical 'amt-scale float32 overflow' bug this file's own comment describes (coverage ~0.49 at d=5): with 1e8-1e11 magnitude float32 input, interior coverage is now >=0.95, confirming the float64-upcast fix holds.

findings.title: cross_zscore's fixed EPS=1e-9 denominator floor is swamped by float32 rounding noise at amount-scale magnitudes, producing spurious +-1 output instead of the mathematically-required 0
findings.summary: cross_zscore computes z=(x-mean_d)/(std_d+EPS) with EPS=1e-9 imported from alphacube.operators.common -- a constant that does not scale with the input's own magnitude. AlphaCube's cube store is float32 (src/alphacube/store.py: 'one float32 (S,D,M) mmap per field'), and this file's own cross_ema comment documents 'the size of a traded amount (1e8 and more)' as a realistic magnitude for exactly the 'amount/level' fields this docstring says cross_zscore is for. At that magnitude in float32, the rounding error in computing mean_d/std_d from a window of identical or near-identical values is many orders of magnitude larger than EPS=1e-9, so for any window whose true day-to-day coefficient of variation is below roughly 1e-6 (a suspended, locked-limit, or just thinly-and-steadily-traded stock), the numerator (x-mean) and denominator (std) become two independently-noisy near-zero floats whose ratio lands near +-1 -- a plausible-looking, non-NaN z-score value -- instead of the 0 the docstring guarantees for a constant window. The NaN/finite pattern itself stays correct; only the value is wrong, which makes this silent.
findings.failure_scenario: D=10 trading days, window d=3, one stock, x constant at 1.5e9 every day (plausible Amt-level value). Running `cross_zscore(torch.tensor(np.full((10,1), 1.5e9), dtype=torch.float32), 3).numpy()[:,0]` returns `[nan, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]` -- a constant stream of 1.0 from day 2 onward. The same call with `dtype=torch.float64` on the identical input returns `[nan, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]`, matching the docstring (mean_d==x[t] and std_d==0 for a constant window, so z must be exactly 0). This is not limited to bit-exact constants: feeding a genuinely random, low-dispersion Amt-like series (base=5e8, i.i.d. relative jitter sigma=1e-7, D=40, d=10, float32) gives a z-range of [-1.94, 1.45], while float64 on the identical input gives [-1.99, 2.20] -- a qualitatively different, uninformative distribution (z-scores are scale-invariant, so the true answer should be essentially unchanged as sigma shrinks). The effect vanishes once the window's coefficient of variation exceeds roughly 1e-5 (at jitter sigma=1e-3 on the same base, max|float32-float64| <= 1.7e-4), so it specifically targets large-magnitude, low-dispersion windows -- i.e. the suspension-adjacent / locked-limit / thinly-traded 'Amt' or 'Volume' segments this A-share project's data routinely contains.
findings.suggested_fix: Scale the stabilizing epsilon to the window's own magnitude instead of the fixed, magnitude-unaware EPS=1e-9 -- the same fix this file already uses for in_madz/cross_madz ('1e-6 * median.abs()', explicitly motivated there by this exact failure mode: 'unlike a rolling kurtosis whose absolute epsilon ... crushes low-priced stocks'). E.g. change line 218 from `torch.sqrt(var) + EPS` to `torch.sqrt(var) + EPS + 1e-6 * m.abs()`, and/or treat the window as degenerate (output exactly 0, not a noise-driven ratio) whenever std_d is not meaningfully larger than mean_d's own floating-point ULP. Upcasting the computation to float64 internally before casting back (mirroring cross_ema's `x.to(torch.float64)` a few lines above in this same file) would also push the breakdown magnitude from ~1e9 out past the realistic range of any field in this cube, though the relative-epsilon fix is the more robust one since it also covers float64 callers at even larger magnitudes.
